dependent_variable.name: ACCY
dependent_variable.definition: Analyst forecast accuracy: the negative absolute difference between the mean I/B/E/S consensus forecast for period t earnings and actual I/B/E/S earnings per share before extraordinary items at t, scaled by stock price at end of t−1. The consensus is formed from forecasts announced between two months before the actual earnings announcement and three days before it; each analyst contributes only their most recent forecast within the window.

evidence.quote: Equation (2): ACCY_t = (-1)*abs(FORECAST_t^(t-1) - EPS_t)/PRICE_(t-1).
the mean I/B/E/S consensus forecast of period t earnings made during the period starting two months before the corresponding actual earnings announcement and ending three days before the announcement
actual earnings per share before extraordinary items at time t, taken from I/B/E/S
the stock price at the end of period t
We remove the influence of stale forecasts by using only the most recent forecast for the calculation of the mean if an analyst announces multiple forecasts during the period.

statistics.units: Negative absolute forecast error scaled by stock price at t−1 (ratio scale).

review_notes: Source-first scope: retain the final full specification in Table 4 (forecast accuracy) and Table 5 (forecast dispersion). The authors state that audit quality is associated with both forecast accuracy and dispersion, formulate H1 and H2 for these two parallel outcome properties, and include both in the multivariate main results. For each outcome, column (6) is the final specification with AUDITOR, ISPEC, their interaction, all outcome-specific controls, the inverse Mills ratio, and year dummies.

Exclude Table 3 univariate comparisons, the sensitivity analyses, year-by-year/Fama–MacBeth checks, and later sample-split equations (5)–(6); those are preliminary comparisons, robustness checks, or follow-up heterogeneity analyses. Retain the first-stage auditor-choice probit only because its fitted results generate INVMR used in both Table 4 and Table 5.
